title: Ch. 3 Notes: Spread
source: Variance is the average squared distance from the mean. Because each distance is squared before averaging, variance is measured in squared units, such as cm squared.
The standard deviation is the square root of the variance. Taking the square root undoes the squaring, so the standard deviation is in the original units of the data.
The standard deviation is easier to interpret because it is in original units. A standard deviation of 4 cm means typical scores sit about 4 cm from the mean.

The range is the difference between the largest and smallest value. The interquartile range, or IQR, is the spread of the middle half of the data. Both describe spread, but neither uses every data point the way variance and standard deviation do.
